docs.title: nowcastbaselines
docs.text:
The random walk and the random walk nowcast, for weekly counts revised as later releases report more cases.

nowcastbaselines is the package in packages/nowcastbaselines of the repository, and builds on nowcastutils (Packages).

docs.title: Install
docs.text: uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/nowcastbaselines"

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
We make a small outbreak in two places, reported with a delay, and forecast its weekly counts with both baselines.

The data are daily onsets by release: each release (vintage) lists every onset day up to its cut-off with the cases reported by then.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
days = pd.date_range("2026-01-04", "2026-04-25")
final = {
    place: rng.poisson(30 * scale * np.exp(0.01 * np.arange(days.size)))
    for place, scale in (("A-1", 1.0), ("A-2", 0.6))
}
releases = pd.date_range("2026-03-07", "2026-04-25", freq="7D")
rows = []
for release in releases:
    for place, counts in final.items():
        for i, day in enumerate(days[days <= release]):
            # Older days are more completely reported.
            age = (release - day).days
            reported = rng.binomial(counts[i], 1 - np.exp(-age / 6))
            rows.append((release, place, day, reported))
daily = pd.DataFrame(
    rows, columns=["vintage", "location", "onset_date", "observed"]
).assign(imputed=0)
for col in ("vintage", "onset_date"):
    daily[col] = daily[col].dt.date.astype(str)
daily["cutoff"] = daily["vintage"]

The weekly counts of each release, by week ending on Saturday, are the forecast target.

onset = pd.to_datetime(daily["onset_date"])
saturday = onset + pd.to_timedelta((5 - onset.dt.weekday) % 7, unit="D")
target = (
    daily.assign(target_end_date=saturday.dt.date.astype(str))
    .groupby(
        ["vintage", "location", "target_end_date", "cutoff"], as_index=False
    )[["observed", "imputed"]]
    .sum()
    .assign(kind="real")
)
target["total"] = target["observed"] + target["imputed"]
target["location_name"] = target["location"]

A task is what a model sees at one release: its data, the places and the weeks to forecast. The weeks run from four weeks before the release's reference week, which the data have not yet completed, to three weeks after. Importing nowcastbaselines.randomwalk adds both models to the registry. Each returns 100 sample trajectories for each place and week.

import datetime as dt

import nowcastbaselines.randomwalk  # noqa: F401
from nowcastutils.base import ForecastTask, get_model
from nowcastutils.dates import reference_date_for_vintage

vintage = daily["vintage"].max()
reference = reference_date_for_vintage(vintage)
task = ForecastTask(
    vintage=vintage,
    reference_date=reference,
    kind="real",
    cutoff=vintage,
    target=target.loc[target["vintage"] == vintage].reset_index(drop=True),
    delays=None,
    locations=("A-1", "A-2"),
    target_end_dates=tuple(
        (reference + dt.timedelta(weeks=h)).isoformat() for h in range(-4, 4)
    ),
    seed=1,
    daily_history=daily,
)
forecasts = {
    name: get_model(name).forecast(task)
    for name in ("randomwalk", "randomwalknowcast")
}
for samples in forecasts.values():
    assert list(samples.columns) == [
        "location",
        "target_end_date",
        "sample",
        "value",
    ]
    assert samples.groupby(["location", "target_end_date"]).size().eq(100).all()

The random walk forecasts each place's weekly count on the log scale from its latest complete week. The random walk nowcast first nowcasts the recent weeks, by estimating the reporting delay from how counts grew between releases, then forecasts each nowcast draw with the random walk.

docs.title: nowcastbaselines.randomwalk
docs.text:
The random walk baselines.

Both models run on the hub's daily release snapshots (chain), from one random walk (walk.random_walk). The places form a hierarchy read from their codes (nowcastutils.hierarchy), so a task may be one series or places of any depth below a root, such as provinces and zones or age groups. A place with no rows of its own is the sum of its children (nowcastutils.snapshots.snapshot_arrays), and a task with no places gives no samples.

RandomWalk (randomwalk) starts from the reported count of the latest week judged complete, $\pi \ge 0.95$, where

$$ \pi(w) = \frac{1}{7} \sum_{t \in w} \frac{\mathbb{1}{t \le c}}{G(a(t))} $$

is the share of the week's final count reported, under the delay estimate of chain. Weeks up to the start are returned as reported. Later weeks are walk draws. A task whose targets are not all hub weeks has 7-day sums ending on each target date: the weeks are the blocks of 7 days ending on the cut-off's weekday, sums to the end of a place's start block are as reported, and later sums walk in daily steps from it (_day_walks), as randomwalknowcast's sums after the cut-off do.

RandomWalkNowcast (randomwalknowcast) nowcasts each hub week, with negative binomial new reports on the remaining count (obs). Weeks with data keep their nowcast draws. If the week holding the cut-off is partial, its days after the cut-off add a Poisson draw from that week's walk rate, walked by each sample from its own nowcast of the latest full week at least Settings.start_share reported with at least Settings.start_count cases (_start_weeks). Each sample's completed cut-off week, its nowcast plus that draw, is the base the walk goes on from for the weeks after the cut-off.

The spread of the walk is the standard deviation of the weekly changes of $\log(1 + y)$ in reported counts, over the weeks ending at the start of randomwalk, net of their delta-method Poisson noise (walk.walk_variance). A place whose net variance is 0 or below has no own estimate. The delay, the observation model and the walk spread each use their own estimate where a place has at least 10 cases a week, and otherwise the pooled estimate of the nearest parent that does (pooling). A place with no case in the latest walk_weeks weeks is silent. It is exactly 0 until its first introduction, which comes each week with its pooled probability times the share of the week not yet reported, and then walks from a count drawn from Poisson(1) given at least 1 (introductions.silent_trajectories). In randomwalknowcast a place with no week to start from is quiet (_quiet): it starts at its latest complete week. A silent quiet place draws introductions from there. One with recent cases walks from its mean reported count over the start_window weeks to that week (_level). National is the sum of provinces by sample. Each model raises if the task has no snapshots or no pair of releases within the delay window.

@dataclass
class RandomWalk:
    """Carry the latest complete week forward with growing noise.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Model name.
    settings : Settings
        Delay window, thresholds and the walk's window.
    copula : CopulaSettings
        How rho_p is estimated (`copula.estimate_rho`).
    fit_diagnostics : list of dict
        One row per place from the last forecast: the start week, the
        errors behind the spread and the source of the delay, spread and
        walk.
    keep_variants : bool
        Keep the last forecast's unpaired draws, for `unpaired`.
    copula_fit : dict or None
        The copula of the last forecast: `model`, `origin`, `n_scores` and
        `copula.estimate_rho`'s `rho_provinces`, `n_pairs` and `fallback`,
        with `reason` where it fell back, or None where there are no
        provinces to pair (a zone task).
    """

    name: str = "randomwalk"
    settings: Settings = field(default_factory=Settings)
    copula: CopulaSettings = field(default_factory=CopulaSettings)
    fit_diagnostics: list[dict[str, object]] = field(default_factory=list)
    keep_variants: bool = field(default=False, repr=False)
    copula_fit: dict[str, object] | None = field(
        init=False, default=None, repr=False
    )
    needs_snapshots: ClassVar[bool] = True
    _snap: SnapshotArrays | None = field(init=False, default=None, repr=False)
    _fits: dict[tuple[int, bool], DelayFit | None] = field(
        init=False, default_factory=dict, repr=False
    )

    def pair(
        self,
        origin: Origin,
        task: ForecastTask,
        values: np.ndarray,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Pair the provinces' draws `[S, L, H]` within each week.

        rho_p is estimated from the normal scores of the model's own
        nowcasts at earlier releases (`copula.error_scores`), shrunk to the
        prior (`copula.estimate_rho`), and the draws are paired by it
        (`copula.pair_walks`). A task with no province, a place one level
        below its root, is left unpaired.
        """
        if self.keep_variants:
            self._unpaired = values
            self._kept_origin = origin
        locations = tuple(origin.snap.locations)
        if not any(depth(c) == 1 for c in task.locations):
            self.copula_fit = None
            return values
        scores, reason = self._error_scores(origin, task)
        c = self.copula
        fit = estimate_rho(scores, c.prior, c.weight, max_rho=c.max_rho)
        self.copula_fit = {
            "model": self.name,
            "origin": task.vintage,
            "n_scores": len(scores),
            **fit,
        }
        if fit["fallback"]:
            reason = reason or "no two provinces scored in the same week"
            self.copula_fit["reason"] = reason
            logger.warning(
                "%s at %s: rho_p falls back to the prior %g (%s).",
                self.name,
                task.vintage,
                c.prior,
                reason,
            )
        rng = task.rng(self.name, "copula")
        rho = float(fit["rho_provinces"])
        return pair_walks(values, locations, rho, rng)

    def unpaired(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return the last forecast's draws before pairing.

        Needs `keep_variants`. The draws are the forecast's own, so only
        their pairing differs.
        """
        weeks, rows, task = self._kept_frame
        return frame(task, weeks, self._unpaired, rows)

    def paired_with(
        self, copula: CopulaSettings
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, object] | None]:
        """Return the last forecast's draws paired under other settings.

        Needs `keep_variants`. The draws are the forecast's own, so only
        their pairing differs, as the release backtest compares them
        (`bdbvhub.pairing.bdbv_candidates`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        copula : CopulaSettings
            The settings to pair by.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            The samples.
        dict or None
            The copula record, as `copula_fit`.
        """
        weeks, rows, task = self._kept_frame
        other = replace(self, copula=copula, keep_variants=False)
        values = other.pair(self._kept_origin, task, self._unpaired)
        return frame(task, weeks, values, rows), other.copula_fit

    def _error_scores(
        self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, str | None]:
        """Return the normal scores of the model's own earlier nowcasts.

        With the reason there are none, if so.
        """
        if origin.errors is None:
            try:
                _add_spread(origin)
            except (ValueError, FloatingPointError, np.linalg.LinAlgError) as e:
                return pd.DataFrame(), f"the earlier nowcasts failed: {e}"
        errors, size = origin.errors, origin.size
        if errors is None or size is None or not errors.releases:
            return pd.DataFrame(), "no earlier release to score"
        snap = origin.snap
        at = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(snap.releases)}
        ages = np.array(
            [snap.cut[origin.o] - snap.cut[at[r]] for r in errors.releases]
        )
        scores = error_scores(
            errors.added,
            errors.remaining,
            errors.valid,
            size,
            list(errors.releases),
            ages,
            tuple(snap.locations),
            self.name,
            task.seed,
            self.copula.window_weeks,
        )
        return scores, None

    def settings_for(self, task: ForecastTask) -> Settings:
        """Return the settings for `task`: its study `max_delay`, if any.

        A task's `max_delay` (`ForecastTask.max_delay`, BDBV's study $D$)
        replaces the settings' own.
        """
        if task.max_delay is None:
            return self.settings
        return dataclasses.replace(self.settings, max_delay=int(task.max_delay))

    def snapshots(self, task: ForecastTask) -> SnapshotArrays:
        """Return the task's release snapshots as arrays.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task. Its `daily_history` holds the release snapshots.

        Returns
        -------
        SnapshotArrays
            The snapshots up to the task's vintage.

        Raises
        ------
        MissingSnapshots
            If the task has no release snapshots.
        """
        _clear_caches(task)
        daily = task.daily_history
        if daily is None or daily.empty:
            raise MissingSnapshots(
                f"{self.name} needs daily release snapshots, and the task "
                f"for {task.vintage} has none."
            )
        return snapshot_arrays(daily, task.vintage, task.locations)

    def origin_at(self, task: ForecastTask, errors: bool) -> Origin:
        """Fit the delays and the walk at the task's vintage.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task. Its `daily_history` holds the release snapshots.
        errors : bool
            Also fit the nowcast errors, which `RandomWalkNowcast` needs.

        Returns
        -------
        Origin
            The fit at the task's vintage.

        Raises
        ------
        MissingSnapshots
            If the task has no release snapshots.
        """
        return build_origin(
            self.snapshots(task), self.settings_for(task), errors
        )

    def rows(self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask) -> list[int]:
        """Return the origin's row of each of the task's places.

        Parameters
        ----------
        origin : Origin
            The fit, from `origin_at`.
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        list of int
            Row indices, in the order of `task.locations`.
        """
        pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(origin.snap.locations)}
        return [pos[c] for c in task.locations]

    def _diagnostics(
        self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask, start: np.ndarray
    ) -> None:
        rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for loc, i in zip(task.locations, self.rows(origin, task), strict=True):
            n_err = None if origin.obs_n is None else int(origin.obs_n[i, 0])
            obs_src = (
                None
                if origin.obs_source is None
                else _label(origin, int(origin.obs_source[i, 0]))
            )
            rows.append(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "start_week": origin.snap.week_ends[int(start[i])],
                    "n_err": n_err,
                    "delay_source": _label(origin, int(origin.fit.source[i])),
                    "obs_source": obs_src,
                    "sigma_source": _label(origin, int(origin.sigma_source[i])),
                }
            )
        self.fit_diagnostics = rows

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return random walk trajectories for a task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The data and weeks to forecast. Its `daily_history` holds the
            release snapshots.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value`.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            If the task has no snapshots, no pair of releases within
            the delay window, or a place with no week that is 95 per cent
            complete (`NoCompleteWeek`).

        Examples
        --------
        >>> from bdbvhub.models import get_model
        >>> samples = get_model("randomwalk").forecast(task)
        >>> samples.groupby(["location", "target_end_date"])["value"].median()
        """
        if not task.locations:
            return frame(task, [], np.zeros((task.n_samples, 0, 0)), [])
        ends = pd.to_datetime(list(task.target_end_dates))
        if (ends.day_of_week != HUB_WEEKDAY).any():
            return self._rolling(task)
        origin = self.origin_at(task, errors=False)
        weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
        n_all, n = len(weeks), task.n_samples
        n_loc = len(origin.snap.locations)
        start = _complete_start(origin)
        x0 = origin.reported[np.arange(n_loc), start]
        _, y = _walks(
            _key(task),
            np.repeat(x0[:, None], n, axis=1),
            origin,
            start,
            n_all,
            origin.silent,
        )
        values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
        for loc in range(n_loc):
            for u in range(n_all):
                if u <= start[loc]:
                    values[:, loc, u] = origin.reported[loc, u]
                else:
                    values[:, loc, u] = y[loc, :, u - start[loc] - 1]
        values = self.pair(origin, task, values)
        self._diagnostics(origin, task, start)
        self._kept_frame = (weeks, self.rows(origin, task), task)
        return frame(task, weeks, values, self.rows(origin, task))

    def _block_origin(
        self, task: ForecastTask, period: int, end: int, errors: bool
    ) -> Origin:
        """Return the fit of the blocks of `period` days ending `end`."""
        snap = self._snap
        assert snap is not None
        return build_origin(
            blocks(snap, period, end),
            self.settings_for(task),
            errors,
            self._shared_delay,
        )

    def _shared_delay(
        self,
        snap: SnapshotArrays,  # noqa: ARG002 - the blocks, as `DelayFn` gives
        r: int,
        settings: Settings,
        longer: bool = False,
    ) -> DelayFit | None:
        """Fit the delay on the hub weeks' snapshots, once per release."""
        key = (r, longer)
        if key not in self._fits:
            assert self._snap is not None
            self._fits[key] = fit_delay(self._snap, r, settings, longer)
        return self._fits[key]

    def _start(self, task: ForecastTask) -> None:
        """Hold the task's snapshots and clear the delay fits."""
        self._snap = self.snapshots(task)
        self._fits = {}

    def _rolling(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return draws of the 7-day sums ending on each target date.

        The weeks are the blocks of 7 days ending on the cut-off's weekday,
        with the delay fitted on the hub weeks (`_shared_delay`). A sum
        ending on or before the end of a place's latest complete block is
        as reported. Later sums walk in daily steps from that block's
        reported sum (`_day_walks`), with the steps of the reported 7-day
        sums ending each day to each place's start (`_daily_steps`).
        """
        self._start(task)
        snap = self._snap
        assert snap is not None
        cut = snap.days[snap.cut[-1]].date()
        origin = self._block_origin(task, 7, cut.weekday(), False)
        start = _complete_start(origin)
        n_loc, n = len(snap.locations), task.n_samples
        targets = list(task.target_end_dates)
        x0 = origin.reported[np.arange(n_loc), start]
        lag = np.array(
            [
                [(as_date(d) - as_date(origin.snap.week_ends[s])).days
                 for d in targets]
                for s in start
            ]
        )  # fmt: skip
        days = origin.snap.days
        ends = np.array(
            [(as_date(origin.snap.week_ends[s]) - days[0].date()).days
             for s in start]
        )  # fmt: skip
        sums = _rolling_sums(origin.snap.counts[:, origin.o, :])
        steps = _daily_steps(sums, days[0].weekday(), ends, origin)
        y = _day_walks(
            _key(task),
            np.repeat(x0[None, :], n, axis=0),
            origin,
            max(int(lag.max()), 1),
            origin.silent,
            steps,
            (cut.weekday() + 1) % 7,
        )
        sums = _reported_sums(snap, targets)
        values = np.empty((n, n_loc, len(targets)))
        for loc in range(n_loc):
            for j, k in enumerate(lag[loc]):
                values[:, loc, j] = sums[loc, j] if k <= 0 else y[:, loc, k - 1]
        values = self.pair(origin, task, values)
        self._diagnostics(origin, task, start)
        rows = self.rows(origin, task)
        self._kept_frame = (targets, rows, task)
        return frame(task, targets, values, rows)

def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return random walk trajectories for a task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The data and weeks to forecast. Its `daily_history` holds the
        release snapshots.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value`.

    Raises
    ------
    ModelUnavailableError
        If the task has no snapshots, no pair of releases within
        the delay window, or a place with no week that is 95 per cent
        complete (`NoCompleteWeek`).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from bdbvhub.models import get_model
    >>> samples = get_model("randomwalk").forecast(task)
    >>> samples.groupby(["location", "target_end_date"])["value"].median()
    """
    if not task.locations:
        return frame(task, [], np.zeros((task.n_samples, 0, 0)), [])
    ends = pd.to_datetime(list(task.target_end_dates))
    if (ends.day_of_week != HUB_WEEKDAY).any():
        return self._rolling(task)
    origin = self.origin_at(task, errors=False)
    weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
    n_all, n = len(weeks), task.n_samples
    n_loc = len(origin.snap.locations)
    start = _complete_start(origin)
    x0 = origin.reported[np.arange(n_loc), start]
    _, y = _walks(
        _key(task),
        np.repeat(x0[:, None], n, axis=1),
        origin,
        start,
        n_all,
        origin.silent,
    )
    values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
    for loc in range(n_loc):
        for u in range(n_all):
            if u <= start[loc]:
                values[:, loc, u] = origin.reported[loc, u]
            else:
                values[:, loc, u] = y[loc, :, u - start[loc] - 1]
    values = self.pair(origin, task, values)
    self._diagnostics(origin, task, start)
    self._kept_frame = (weeks, self.rows(origin, task), task)
    return frame(task, weeks, values, self.rows(origin, task))

@dataclass
class RandomWalkNowcast(RandomWalk):
    """The random walk run forward from a daily nowcast of the recent weeks.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Model name.
    error_days : int, default 7
        Days in a block of the observation model. With 7, a task of hub
        weeks is nowcast by week and one whose targets are other days by
        blocks of 7 days ending on each, each with its own observation
        model (baselinenowcast's 7-day rolling `ref_time_aggregator`).
        With 1, the observation model is fitted on daily counts and the
        7-day sums are sums of daily draws.
    delay_summary : pandas.DataFrame or None
        The delay of the last forecast
        (`baselinenowcast.nowcast.delay_summary`), which maps its final
        counts to what later releases show.
    """

    name: str = "randomwalknowcast"
    error_days: int = 7
    delay_summary: pd.DataFrame | None = field(
        init=False, default=None, repr=False
    )

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return random walk trajectories from a nowcast for a task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The data and weeks to forecast. Its `daily_history` holds the
            release snapshots.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value`.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            If the task has no snapshots, or no pair of releases within
            the delay window.
        """
        if not task.locations:
            return frame(task, [], np.zeros((task.n_samples, 0, 0)), [])
        ends = pd.to_datetime(list(task.target_end_dates))
        if self.error_days != 7 or (ends.weekday != HUB_WEEKDAY).any():
            return self._rolling(task)
        origin = self.origin_at(task, errors=True)
        values, weeks = self.trajectories(origin, task, origin.point)
        values = self.pair(origin, task, values)
        self.delay_summary = delay_summary(origin, self.name, task.vintage)
        self._diagnostics(
            origin,
            task,
            _start_weeks(origin),
        )
        self._kept_frame = (weeks, self.rows(origin, task), task)
        return frame(task, weeks, values, self.rows(origin, task))

    def _block_draws(
        self,
        task: ForecastTask,
        period: int,
        end: int = HUB_WEEKDAY,
        weekdays: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[Origin, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
        """Return the draws of each block of `period` days ending `end`.

        The delay is fitted once, on the hub weeks' snapshots, and shared
        by every block (`_shared_delay`); the observation model, the walk
        and the copula are fitted on the blocks. With `weekdays`, blocks
        of one day walk in days (`_nowcast_steps`).
        """
        origin = self._block_origin(task, period, end, True)
        if weekdays:
            origin = replace(origin, steps=_nowcast_steps(origin))
        values, labels = self.trajectories(origin, task, origin.point)
        values = self.pair(origin, task, values)
        return origin, {w: values[:, :, i] for i, w in enumerate(labels)}

    def _rolling(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return draws of the 7-day sums ending on each target date.

        With `error_days` 7 each sum to the cut-off is a block of 7 days
        ending on its weekday, with its own observation model, as
        baselinenowcast's `ref_time_aggregator` of 7-day rolling sums.
        The sums after the cut-off walk on in daily steps from each
        sample's sum ending on the cut-off (`_walk_days`), so they carry
        no weekday cycle. With 1, the
        sums are of draws of daily counts, whose observation model is
        fitted on days.
        """
        self._start(task)
        targets = list(task.target_end_dates)
        draws: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        if self.error_days == 1:
            origin, days = self._block_draws(task, 1, weekdays=True)
            labels = list(days)
            x = np.stack([days[d] for d in labels], axis=-1)
            c = np.concatenate(
                [np.zeros((*x.shape[:2], 1)), np.cumsum(x, axis=-1)], axis=-1
            )
            week = c[..., 7:] - c[..., :-7]
            draws = {d: week[..., i] for i, d in enumerate(labels[6:])}
        else:
            snap = self._snap
            assert snap is not None
            cut = snap.days[snap.cut[-1]].date()
            past = [d for d in targets if as_date(d) <= cut]
            ends = {as_date(d).weekday() for d in past} - {cut.weekday()}
            for end in sorted(ends):
                _, got = self._block_draws(task, 7, end)
                draws.update({d: got[d] for d in past if d in got})
            origin, walk = self._block_draws(task, 7, cut.weekday())
            draws.update({d: walk[d] for d in past if d in walk})
            ahead = [d for d in targets if as_date(d) > cut]
            if ahead:
                draws.update(
                    self._walk_days(
                        origin, task, walk[cut.isoformat()], cut, ahead
                    )
                )
        self.delay_summary = delay_summary(origin, self.name, task.vintage)
        rows = self.rows(origin, task)
        n = task.n_samples
        values = np.stack(
            [draws.get(d, np.zeros((n, len(origin.snap.locations))))
             for d in targets],
            axis=-1,
        )  # fmt: skip
        self._kept_frame = (targets, rows, task)
        return frame(task, targets, values, rows)

    def _walk_days(
        self,
        origin: Origin,
        task: ForecastTask,
        start: np.ndarray,
        cut: dt.date,
        days: list[str],
    ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        """Walk each sample's 7-day sum ending on the cut-off in daily steps.

        The walk is `_day_walks`, and the draws are paired as the weekly
        ones (`pair`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        origin : Origin
            The fit of the 7-day blocks ending on the cut-off's weekday.
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.
        start : numpy.ndarray
            Each sample's sum ending on the cut-off, `[S, L]`.
        cut : datetime.date
            The cut-off.
        days : list of str
            The days after the cut-off to return, ISO format.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            Each day's draws, `[S, L]`.
        """
        h = max((as_date(d) - cut).days for d in days)
        day = self._block_origin(task, 1, HUB_WEEKDAY, False)
        counts = _day_walks(
            jax.random.fold_in(_key(task), 7),
            start,
            origin,
            h,
            _quiet(origin),
            _nowcast_steps(day, rolling=True),
            (cut.weekday() + 1) % 7,
        )
        values = self.pair(origin, task, counts)
        return {d: values[:, :, (as_date(d) - cut).days - 1] for d in days}

    def daily_quantiles(
        self, task: ForecastTask, levels: tuple[float, ...]
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return quantiles of each target date's count, by place.

        The draws are of blocks of one day, with the observation model
        fitted on daily counts, and the walk steps a day, into each
        weekday with its mean and the spread of `_nowcast_steps`. The
        country is
        the sum of the provinces by sample (`add_national`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.
        levels : tuple of float
            Quantile levels.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `location`, `date`, `quantile` and `value`.
        """
        self._start(task)
        origin, days = self._block_draws(task, 1, weekdays=True)
        targets = list(task.target_end_dates)
        n = task.n_samples
        values = np.stack(
            [days.get(d, np.zeros((n, len(origin.snap.locations))))
             for d in targets],
            axis=-1,
        )  # fmt: skip
        draws = add_national(
            frame(task, targets, values, self.rows(origin, task))
        )
        q = (
            draws.groupby(["location", "target_end_date"])["value"]
            .quantile(np.asarray(levels))
            .rename("value")
            .reset_index()
        )
        return q.rename(
            columns={"target_end_date": "date", "level_2": "quantile"}
        )[["location", "date", "quantile", "value"]]

    def trajectories(
        self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask, point: np.ndarray
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str]]:
        """Return trajectories from a nowcast with mean `point`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        origin : Origin
            The fit at the task's vintage, with its observation model.
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.
        point : numpy.ndarray
            Mean weekly nowcast, `[L, W]`. The model's own is
            `origin.point`. A later release's expected count gives the
            prediction scored in the backtest.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple
            Samples `[S, L, H]` for every hub week from the first data
            week to the last target, and those weeks.
        """
        snap = origin.snap
        assert origin.size is not None
        weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
        n_data, n_all, n = snap.n_weeks, len(weeks), task.n_samples
        n_loc = len(snap.locations)
        k_n = origin.size.shape[1]
        back = snap.cut_week(origin.o) - np.arange(n_data)
        # Weeks older than the fitted ones have nothing to come.
        k = np.clip(back, 0, k_n - 1)
        key_x, key_walk, key_part, key_ahead = jax.random.split(_key(task), 4)
        shape = (n, *point.shape)
        reported = jnp.broadcast_to(
            jnp.asarray(origin.reported, jnp.float32), shape
        )
        nowcast = np.asarray(
            sample_count(
                key_x,
                reported,
                jnp.maximum(jnp.asarray(point, jnp.float32) - reported, 0.0),
                jnp.broadcast_to(
                    jnp.asarray(origin.size[:, k], jnp.float32), shape
                ),
            ),
            np.float64,
        )
        # Each sample walks on from its own nowcast of the start week.
        cw = snap.cut_week(origin.o)
        w0 = _start_weeks(origin)
        quiet = _quiet(origin)
        rows = np.arange(n_loc)
        # Only silent places draw introductions: one with recent cases has
        # a level to walk from.
        x0 = nowcast[:, rows, w0].T
        low = quiet & ~origin.silent
        x0[low] = _level(origin)[low, None]
        # A walk in days steps into each day's weekday (`Origin.steps`).
        day0 = as_date(snap.week_ends[0]).weekday()
        lam, y = _walks(
            key_walk,
            x0,
            origin,
            w0,
            n_all,
            origin.silent,
            origin.steps,
            (day0 + w0 + 1) % 7,
        )
        # Days of the cut-off week after the cut-off are drawn from the
        # walk's rate that week. A partial cut-off week's start week is the
        # week before it when that week meets the start rule, so the rate
        # is one step from each sample's nowcast of the week before, and
        # otherwise steps on from the latest earlier week that meets it.
        cut = int(snap.cut[origin.o])
        miss = int(np.flatnonzero(snap.week == cw).max()) - cut
        at_cw = np.clip(cw - w0 - 1, 0, n_all - 1)
        part = np.asarray(
            jax.random.poisson(
                key_part,
                jnp.asarray(
                    lam[rows, :, at_cw] * miss / snap.period, jnp.float32
                ),
            ),
            dtype=np.float64,
        )  # [L, S]
        # Each sample's completed cut-off week is the base for the weeks
        # after it, from which the walk goes on.
        done = nowcast[:, rows, cw].T + np.where(miss > 0, part, 0.0)
        h = n_all - cw - 1
        _, ahead = _walk(
            jax.random.split(key_ahead, n_loc),
            done,
            origin.sigma,
            max(h, 1),
            origin.steps,
            np.full(n_loc, (day0 + cw + 1) % 7),
        )
        ahead = np.asarray(ahead, np.float64)[:, :, :h]
        values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
        for loc in range(n_loc):
            s = int(w0[loc])
            if quiet[loc]:
                # A quiet place is its reported counts, then its walk or
                # introductions.
                values[:, loc, : s + 1] = origin.reported[loc, : s + 1]
                values[:, loc, s + 1 :] = y[loc, :, : n_all - s - 1]
                continue
            values[:, loc, :cw] = nowcast[:, loc, :cw]
            values[:, loc, cw] = done[loc]
            values[:, loc, cw + 1 :] = ahead[loc]
        return values, weeks

    assert origin.size is not None
    weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
    n_data, n_all, n = snap.n_weeks, len(weeks), task.n_samples
    n_loc = len(snap.locations)
    k_n = origin.size.shape[1]
    back = snap.cut_week(origin.o) - np.arange(n_data)
    # Weeks older than the fitted ones have nothing to come.
    k = np.clip(back, 0, k_n - 1)
    key_x, key_walk, key_part, key_ahead = jax.random.split(_key(task), 4)
    shape = (n, *point.shape)
    reported = jnp.broadcast_to(
        jnp.asarray(origin.reported, jnp.float32), shape
    )
    nowcast = np.asarray(
        sample_count(
            key_x,
            reported,
            jnp.maximum(jnp.asarray(point, jnp.float32) - reported, 0.0),
            jnp.broadcast_to(
                jnp.asarray(origin.size[:, k], jnp.float32), shape
            ),
        ),
        np.float64,
    )
    # Each sample walks on from its own nowcast of the start week.
    cw = snap.cut_week(origin.o)
    w0 = _start_weeks(origin)
    quiet = _quiet(origin)
    rows = np.arange(n_loc)
    # Only silent places draw introductions: one with recent cases has
    # a level to walk from.
    x0 = nowcast[:, rows, w0].T
    low = quiet & ~origin.silent
    x0[low] = _level(origin)[low, None]
    # A walk in days steps into each day's weekday (`Origin.steps`).
    day0 = as_date(snap.week_ends[0]).weekday()
    lam, y = _walks(
        key_walk,
        x0,
        origin,
        w0,
        n_all,
        origin.silent,
        origin.steps,
        (day0 + w0 + 1) % 7,
    )
    # Days of the cut-off week after the cut-off are drawn from the
    # walk's rate that week. A partial cut-off week's start week is the
    # week before it when that week meets the start rule, so the rate
    # is one step from each sample's nowcast of the week before, and
    # otherwise steps on from the latest earlier week that meets it.
    cut = int(snap.cut[origin.o])
    miss = int(np.flatnonzero(snap.week == cw).max()) - cut
    at_cw = np.clip(cw - w0 - 1, 0, n_all - 1)
    part = np.asarray(
        jax.random.poisson(
            key_part,
            jnp.asarray(
                lam[rows, :, at_cw] * miss / snap.period, jnp.float32
            ),
        ),
        dtype=np.float64,
    )  # [L, S]
    # Each sample's completed cut-off week is the base for the weeks
    # after it, from which the walk goes on.
    done = nowcast[:, rows, cw].T + np.where(miss > 0, part, 0.0)
    h = n_all - cw - 1
    _, ahead = _walk(
        jax.random.split(key_ahead, n_loc),
        done,
        origin.sigma,
        max(h, 1),
        origin.steps,
        np.full(n_loc, (day0 + cw + 1) % 7),
    )
    ahead = np.asarray(ahead, np.float64)[:, :, :h]
    values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
    for loc in range(n_loc):
        s = int(w0[loc])
        if quiet[loc]:
            # A quiet place is its reported counts, then its walk or
            # introductions.
            values[:, loc, : s + 1] = origin.reported[loc, : s + 1]
            values[:, loc, s + 1 :] = y[loc, :, : n_all - s - 1]
            continue
        values[:, loc, :cw] = nowcast[:, loc, :cw]
        values[:, loc, cw] = done[loc]
        values[:, loc, cw + 1 :] = ahead[loc]
    return values, weeks

def frame(
    task: ForecastTask, weeks: list[str], values: np.ndarray, rows: list[int]
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return sample rows from `values` of shape `[S, L, H]`.

    A task with no places gives no rows.

    if not task.locations:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS))
    col = {w: i for i, w in enumerate(weeks)}
    targets = list(task.target_end_dates)
    n = values.shape[0]
    frames = []
    for loc, row in zip(task.locations, rows, strict=True):
        picked = np.column_stack(
            [
                values[:, row, col[w]] if w in col else np.zeros(n)
                for w in targets
            ]
        )
        frames.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "target_end_date": np.tile(targets, n),
                    "sample": np.repeat(np.arange(1, n + 1), len(targets)),
                    "value": np.maximum(np.round(picked), 0.0).reshape(-1),
                }
            )
        )
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)[list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)]

docs.text:
The random walk, one function for both models.

From start value $x_i$ per sample, for $h \ge 1$,

$$ \log(1 + \lambda_i(h)) = \max\Big(0, \log(1 + x_i) + \sum_{j=1}^{h} \epsilon_{i,j}\Big), \quad \epsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2), $$

$$ y_i(h) \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i(h)). $$

Steps are cumulative within a sample, so each sample is one trajectory.

The spread $\sigma$ comes from the weekly changes $\Delta_t$ of $\log(1 + y_t)$ in reported counts, net of their Poisson noise,

$$ \sigma^2 = \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\Delta_t) - \overline{v(y_{t-1}) + v(y_t)}, \quad v(y) = \frac{y}{(1 + y)^2}, $$

where $v$ is the delta-method variance of $\log(1 + Y)$ for $Y \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$, $\lambda / (1 + \lambda)^2$, with the observed count for $\lambda$ (walk_variance). The walk draws its Poisson counts on top, so the noise is not counted twice.

A walk in days (DailySteps) has $\epsilon_{i,j} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{d(j)}, \sigma^2)$, where $d(j)$ is the weekday of step $j$'s day. $\mu_d$ is the mean change into weekday $d$ (weekday_means), centred so the seven sum to 0: the walk repeats the weekly pattern and has no drift. $\sigma^2$ is the variance of the changes over 7 days, net of their Poisson noise, over 7 (same_weekday_variance), in which a recurring weekday effect cancels. A walk in weeks has one step type, $\mu = 0$.

def walk_noise(y: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Return the Poisson noise variance of each change of log(1 + y).

    Parameters
    ----------
    y : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly counts, `[W]`.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        $v(y_{t-1}) + v(y_t)$ for each change, `[W - 1]`, with
        $v(y) = y / (1 + y)^2$ the delta-method variance of
        $\log(1 + Y)$ for $Y \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(y)$.
    """
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    v = y / (1.0 + y) ** 2
    return v[1:] + v[:-1]

def walk_variance(changes: np.ndarray, noise: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Return the variance of the walk's steps net of Poisson noise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    changes : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly changes of log(1 + y), `[N]`.
    noise : numpy.ndarray
        Their Poisson noise variances (`walk_noise`), `[N]`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The sample variance of `changes` less the mean of `noise`. It
        may be 0 or below, which says the changes hold no more than
        Poisson noise. NaN with fewer than 2 changes.
    """
    if changes.size < 2:
        return float("nan")
    return float(np.var(changes, ddof=1)) - float(np.mean(noise))

def same_weekday_variance(series: Sequence[np.ndarray]) -> float:
    """Return a daily walk step's variance from same-weekday changes.

    The changes of log(1 + y) over 7 days of each daily series, pooled
    and net of their Poisson noise (`walk_variance`), over 7: a
    recurring weekday effect cancels in them, and a random walk's
    variance over 7 steps is 7 times a step's.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : sequence of numpy.ndarray
        Daily counts, each `[T]`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        As `walk_variance` gives it, over 7.
    """
    logs = [np.log1p(np.asarray(y, dtype=float)) for y in series]
    noise = [np.asarray(y, dtype=float) for y in series]
    noise = [v / (1.0 + v) ** 2 for v in noise]
    return (
        walk_variance(
            np.concatenate([lg[7:] - lg[:-7] for lg in logs]),
            np.concatenate([v[7:] + v[:-7] for v in noise]),
        )
        / 7.0
    )

def random_walk(
    key: Array,
    x0: Array,
    sigma: Array | float,
    h: int,
    mean: Array | None = None,
) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
    r"""Draw the walk forward on the log scale with Poisson counts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : jax.Array
        Random key.
    x0 : jax.Array
        Start value of each sample, shape `[S]`.
    sigma : float or jax.Array
        Standard deviation of a step, or of each step, `[h]`.
    h : int
        Steps to draw.
    mean : jax.Array, optional
        Mean of each step, `[h]`; without it the steps have mean 0.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of jax.Array
        The rate $\lambda$ and the Poisson count, each `[S, h]`.
    """
    k_step, k_count = jax.random.split(key)
    steps = sigma * jax.random.normal(k_step, (x0.shape[0], h), x0.dtype)
    if mean is not None:
        steps = steps + mean
    level = jnp.log1p(x0)[:, None] + jnp.cumsum(steps, axis=1)
    lam = jnp.expm1(jnp.maximum(level, 0.0))
    return lam, jax.random.poisson(k_count, lam).astype(x0.dtype)

docs.title: nowcastbaselines.pooling
docs.text:
The one own-or-pooled rule.

Places form a hierarchy, zone then province then country. Each node has an own estimate, from its own counts, errors or weekly changes, and a pooled estimate, from its children with a level of at least min_level cases a week. A parent's counts are the sum of its children's, so the parent is not in its own pool unless no child qualifies. A node counts as qualifying when its level is at least min_level, and for the walk spread also when its estimate exists (a net variance above 0). A qualifying node uses its own estimate. Otherwise it uses the pooled estimate of its nearest ancestor that qualifies, else the country's pooled estimate. The delay, the spread of the walk and the observation model all use this rule with one threshold.

def pool_matrix(
    level: np.ndarray, parent: np.ndarray, min_level: float = MIN_LEVEL
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the matrix that sums a node's qualifying children.

    Parameters
    ----------
    level : numpy.ndarray
        Cases a week of each node, `[L]`.
    parent : numpy.ndarray
        Index of each node's parent, or -1, `[L]`.
    min_level : float
        Level at which a child enters its parent's pool.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L, L]`, with entry `[n, m]` 1 if $m$ is a child of $n$ with a
        level of at least `min_level`, or if $m = n$ and no child of $n$
        qualifies.
    """
    n = len(level)
    out = np.zeros((n, n))
    for m in range(n):
        if parent[m] >= 0 and level[m] >= min_level:
            out[parent[m], m] = 1.0
    alone = out.sum(axis=1) == 0
    out[alone, alone] = 1.0
    return out

def source_index(
    level: np.ndarray,
    parent: np.ndarray,
    n_own: np.ndarray | None = None,
    n_pooled: np.ndarray | None = None,
    min_level: float = MIN_LEVEL,
    min_err: int = 1,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the node whose estimate each node uses.

    Parameters
    ----------
    level : numpy.ndarray
        Cases a week of each node, `[L]`.
    parent : numpy.ndarray
        Index of each node's parent, or -1, `[L]`.
    n_own, n_pooled : numpy.ndarray, optional
        Errors behind each node's own and pooled estimates, `[L, K]`.
        Without them, only the level counts and the result is `[L]`.
    min_level : float
        Level at which a node qualifies.
    min_err : int
        Errors a node's estimate needs, where they are given.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Integer index `i`, `[L]` or `[L, K]`. It is an index into the
        own estimates for `i < L` and into the pooled estimates for
        `i >= L`, as `i - L`. Each estimate is gathered with it.
    """
    level = np.asarray(level, dtype=float)
    parent = np.asarray(parent, dtype=int)
    n = level.size
    big = (level >= min_level)[:, None]
    if n_own is None or n_pooled is None:
        ok_own, ok_pool = big, big
    else:
        ok_own = big & (np.asarray(n_own) >= min_err)
        ok_pool = big & (np.asarray(n_pooled) >= min_err)
    k_n = ok_own.shape[1]
    out = np.empty((n, k_n), dtype=int)
    for node in range(n):
        root = node
        while parent[root] >= 0:
            root = parent[root]
        for k in range(k_n):
            if ok_own[node, k]:
                out[node, k] = node
                continue
            a = parent[node]
            while a >= 0 and not ok_pool[a, k]:
                a = parent[a]
            out[node, k] = n + (a if a >= 0 else root)
    return out[:, 0] if n_own is None or n_pooled is None else out

docs.title: nowcastbaselines.introductions
docs.text:
Introductions into places with no recent cases.

A place with no case reported in the latest k weeks is silent (silent_places). It is exactly 0 until its first introduction. An introduction comes each week with probability $q$ times the share of the week not yet reported (introduction_rates). $q$ is the rate of a first case for a place with none yet, and of a re-introduction for a place seen before, over the k weeks to the place's start week. It combines a local rate, pooled over the place and its siblings, and a global rate, pooled over the other places of its level, as independent sources: $q = 1 - (1 - q_l)(1 - q_g)$. It brings a count drawn from Poisson(1) given at least 1, and the place then walks on $\log(1 + y)$ with its walk spread (silent_trajectories).

def silent_places(reported: np.ndarray, cut_week: int, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the places with no case in the `k` weeks to `cut_week`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reported : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly reported counts, `[L, W]`.
    cut_week : int
        Index of the week holding the cut-off.
    k : int
        Weeks without a case.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L]`, true where silent.
    """
    recent = reported[:, max(cut_week - k + 1, 0) : cut_week + 1]
    return np.asarray(recent.sum(axis=1) == 0)

Return each place's weekly probability of an introduction.

A place with no case yet takes the rate of a first case: the weeks with a case over the weeks with none before them. A place seen before takes the rate of a re-introduction: the weeks with a case over the weeks with an earlier case but none in the k weeks before them. Each rate counts the k weeks to each place's start week, the weeks that set the spread of the walk. Only complete weeks before the origin are used. The local rate $q_l$ pools the place and its siblings, the children of its parent, so zones pool within their province. The global rate $q_g$ pools the other places of the same level (zones of the other provinces); provinces and the country have none, so their $q_g = 0$. The two are independent sources, $q = 1 - (1 - q_l)(1 - q_g)$, so $q$ is 0 only where the whole level has no introduction of that kind.

def introduction_rates(
    reported: np.ndarray, start: np.ndarray, parent: np.ndarray, k: int
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Return each place's weekly probability of an introduction.

    A place with no case yet takes the rate of a first case: the weeks
    with a case over the weeks with none before them.
    A place seen before takes the rate of a re-introduction: the weeks
    with a case over the weeks with an earlier case but none in the `k`
    weeks before them.
    Each rate counts the `k` weeks to each place's start week, the weeks
    that set the spread of the walk. Only complete weeks before the
    origin are used.
    The local rate $q_l$ pools the place and its siblings, the children
    of its parent, so zones pool within their province. The global rate
    $q_g$ pools the other places of the same level (zones of the other
    provinces); provinces and the country have none, so their $q_g = 0$.
    The two are independent sources, $q = 1 - (1 - q_l)(1 - q_g)$, so $q$
    is 0 only where the whole level has no introduction of that kind.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reported : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly reported counts, `[L, W]`.
    start : numpy.ndarray
        Start week of each place, `[L]`.
    parent : numpy.ndarray
        Index of each place's parent, or -1, `[L]`.
    k : int
        Weeks counted, and silent weeks before a re-introduction.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L]`, 0 where neither pool has a week at risk with a case.
    """
    pos = reported > 0
    before = np.cumsum(np.pad(pos, ((0, 0), (1, 0))), axis=1)[:, :-1]
    week = np.arange(pos.shape[1])[None, :]
    upto = week <= start[:, None]
    window = upto & (week > start[:, None] - k)
    quiet = np.zeros_like(pos)
    quiet[:, k:] = before[:, k:] == before[:, :-k]
    fresh, seen = upto & (before == 0), upto & quiet & (before > 0)
    first = _pooled(fresh & window, pos, parent)
    again = _pooled(seen & window, pos, parent)
    out: np.ndarray = np.where(pos.any(axis=1), again, first)
    return out

def silent_trajectories(
    key: jax.Array,
    silent: np.ndarray,
    q: np.ndarray,
    unreported: np.ndarray,
    start: np.ndarray,
    sigma: np.ndarray,
    h: int,
    n: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Draw the counts of silent places after their start week.

    A silent place is exactly 0 until its first introduction.
    Week `start + 1 + i` brings one with probability $q$ times the share
    of the week not yet reported, so an introduction is likelier in
    recent weeks, whose cases may still be reported, and has probability
    $q$ in weeks without data.
    The introduction brings a count drawn from Poisson(1) given at least
    1, and the place then walks on $\log(1 + y)$ with spread `sigma`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : jax.Array
        Random key.
    silent : numpy.ndarray
        True where a place is silent, `[L]`.
    q : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly probability of a first case (`introduction_rates`), `[L]`.
    unreported : numpy.ndarray
        Share of each week not yet reported, `[L, W]`.
        Weeks after `W` are wholly unreported.
    start : numpy.ndarray
        Week after which the counts are drawn, `[L]`.
    sigma : numpy.ndarray
        Standard deviation of a weekly walk step, `[L]`.
    h : int
        Weeks to draw.
    n : int
        Samples to draw.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Counts for weeks `start + 1` to `start + h`, `[L, n, h]`, and 0
        for places that are not silent.
    """
    out = np.zeros((silent.size, n, h))
    idx = np.flatnonzero(silent)
    if idx.size == 0:
        return out
    u = start[idx, None] + 1 + np.arange(h)[None, :]
    share = np.take_along_axis(
        np.pad(unreported[idx], ((0, 0), (0, h + 1)), constant_values=1.0),
        u,
        axis=1,
    )
    k_walk, k_intro, k_count = jax.random.split(key, 3)
    v = np.asarray(jax.random.uniform(k_count, (idx.size, n)), np.float64)
    x0 = stats.poisson.ppf(np.exp(-1.0) + v * -np.expm1(-1.0), 1.0)
    keys = jax.random.split(k_walk, idx.size)
    _, drawn = random_walks(
        keys,
        jnp.asarray(x0, jnp.float32),
        jnp.asarray(sigma[idx], jnp.float32),
        h,
    )
    y = np.asarray(drawn, dtype=np.float64)
    hit = np.asarray(jax.random.uniform(k_intro, (idx.size, n, h))) < (
        q[idx, None, None] * share[:, None, :]
    )
    first = np.where(hit.any(axis=2), np.argmax(hit, axis=2), h)
    lag = np.arange(h)[None, None, :] - first[:, :, None]
    # The introduced count is the first week's, and the walk from it
    # gives the weeks after.
    walked = np.take_along_axis(y, np.clip(lag - 1, 0, h - 1), axis=2)
    paths = np.where(lag >= 1, walked, 0.0)
    out[idx] = np.where(lag == 0, x0[:, :, None], paths)
    return out

docs.text:
A Gaussian copula that pairs the walk models' province draws.

randomwalk and randomwalknowcast draw each province on its own, so the country, the sum of the provinces, is too narrow. pair_walks pairs the provinces' draws within each week: each week, each trajectory draws one normal per province with correlation $\rho_p$ between any two, and each cell's draws are reordered across trajectories so they rank as the normals do (the Schaake shuffle, Clark et al. 2004, as ensemble copula coupling uses it, Schefzik et al. 2013). So each cell keeps exactly the draws it had, whether it is nowcast or walking. Weeks are not paired with each other, so a province's own weeks are not kept as one trajectory, and zones and the country are not paired at all. estimate_rho estimates $\rho_p$ from normal scores of a model's own matured errors (error_scores), shrunk towards a prior as a guard for thin windows.

def estimate_rho(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    prior: float = PRIOR,
    weight: float = PRIOR_WEIGHT,
    max_rho: float = MAX_RHO,
) -> dict[str, float | int | bool]:
    r"""Estimate $\rho_p$ from normal scores, with its record.

    $r$ is the Pearson correlation of the scores of every pair of two
    provinces in the same week of one forecast; the country and zones are
    left out. With $n$ pairs and the prior $\rho_0$ the estimate is
    $(n r + w \rho_0) / (n + w)$, the prior's where the pairs give no $r$,
    then floored at zero and capped at `max_rho`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        `error_scores`: `model`, `origin`, `location`,
        `target_end_date` and `z`.
    prior : float
        $\rho_0$.
    weight : float
        $w$, the pairs the prior counts as.
    max_rho : float
        The largest estimate.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `rho_provinces`, `n_pairs` (the pairs behind it, 0 if it fell
        back) and `fallback` (whether it fell back to the prior for want of
        pairs that define it).
    """
    fallback: dict[str, float | int | bool] = {
        "rho_provinces": prior,
        "n_pairs": 0,
        "fallback": True,
    }
    if scores.empty:
        return fallback
    rows = scores.loc[_provinces(scores["location"])]
    key = ["model", "origin", "target_end_date"]
    pairs = rows.merge(rows, on=key, suffixes=("_a", "_b"))
    pairs = pairs.loc[pairs["location_a"] < pairs["location_b"]]
    r = None
    if len(pairs) >= 2:
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            r = np.corrcoef(pairs["z_a"], pairs["z_b"])[0, 1]
        r = float(r) if np.isfinite(r) else None
    if r is None:
        return fallback
    n = len(pairs)
    rho = float(np.clip((n * r + weight * prior) / (n + weight), 0, max_rho))
    return {"rho_provinces": rho, "n_pairs": int(n), "fallback": False}

def error_scores(
    added: np.ndarray,
    remaining: np.ndarray,
    valid: np.ndarray,
    size: np.ndarray,
    releases: list[str],
    ages: np.ndarray,
    locations: tuple[str, ...],
    model: str,
    seed: int,
    window_weeks: int = WINDOW_WEEKS,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    r"""Return normal scores of a model's own nowcasts at earlier releases.

    At each earlier release $r$ the model nowcast the count still to come
    of each place and week back, as a negative binomial with mean
    `remaining` and size $\phi_k$; the origin release reports what came
    (`added`). The score is $\Phi^{-1}$ of the randomised PIT of `added`
    in that distribution, with the uniform drawn from a hash of the seed,
    model, release, place and week back, so a score does not depend on the
    others. Releases more than `window_weeks` weeks before the
    origin are left out, as are cells with no nowcast spread.

    Parameters
    ----------
    added, remaining, valid : numpy.ndarray
        `chain.Errors` fields, `[R, L, K]`.
    size : numpy.ndarray
        Negative binomial size of each place and week back, `[L, K]`.
    releases : list of str
        The releases, `[R]`.
    ages : numpy.ndarray
        Days from each release's cut-off to the origin's, `[R]`.
    locations : tuple of str
        The places, `[L]`.
    model : str
        The model, as the scores' `model`.
    seed : int
        Seed of the uniform draws.
    window_weeks : int
        The latest weeks of releases used.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `model`, `origin` (the release), `location`, `target_end_date`
        (a date 7 days apart per week back, so consecutive weeks pair) and
        `z`, as `estimate_rho` takes them.
    """
    from scipy.stats import nbinom

    cols = ["model", "origin", "location", "target_end_date", "z"]
    keep = np.asarray(ages) <= 7 * window_weeks
    if not keep.any():
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=cols)
    mu = np.asarray(remaining, float)[keep]
    y = np.asarray(added, float)[keep]
    ok = np.asarray(valid, bool)[keep] & (mu > 0)
    phi = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(size, float)[None], mu.shape)
    ok &= np.isfinite(phi) & (phi > 0)
    r, loc, k = np.nonzero(ok)
    if r.size == 0:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=cols)
    n, m, yy = phi[r, loc, k], mu[r, loc, k], np.maximum(y[r, loc, k], 0)
    p = n / (n + m)
    below = nbinom.cdf(yy - 1, n, p)
    at = nbinom.pmf(yy, n, p)
    rel = np.asarray(releases, dtype=object)[keep][r]
    codes = np.asarray(locations, dtype=object)[loc]
    keys = [
        f"{seed}|{model}|{a}|{b}|{c}"
        for a, b, c in zip(rel, codes, k, strict=True)
    ]
    u = (np.array([zlib.crc32(x.encode()) for x in keys]) + 0.5) / 2.0**32
    pit = np.clip(below + u * at, 1e-12, 1 - 1e-12)
    week = pd.Timestamp("2000-01-01") - pd.to_timedelta(7 * k, unit="D")
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "model": model,
            "origin": rel,
            "location": codes,
            "target_end_date": week.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            "z": ndtri(pit),
        }
    )[cols]

def pair_walks(
    values: np.ndarray,
    locations: tuple[str, ...],
    rho: float,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Pair a walk model's province draws within each week.

    Each week, each trajectory draws one normal per place, with
    correlation `rho` between any two, and each province's draws that week
    are reordered to rank as its normals do, whether the province is
    nowcast or walking that week. So every week's provinces are paired,
    but a province's own weeks are not kept as one trajectory, which
    nothing submitted or scored uses. The country and zones keep their
    draws as they are.

    Parameters
    ----------
    values : numpy.ndarray
        Draws `[S, L, H]`.
    locations : tuple of str
        The places' codes.
    rho : float
        $\rho_p$, in [0, 1).
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random generator.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `values` with each province cell's draws reordered across
        trajectories.
    """
    if not 0.0 <= rho < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("rho must be between 0 and 1 (not 1).")
    n, n_places, n_steps = values.shape
    paired = _provinces(locations)
    if not paired.any():
        return values
    z = np.sqrt(rho) * rng.standard_normal((n, 1, n_steps)) + np.sqrt(
        1 - rho
    ) * rng.standard_normal((n, n_places, n_steps))
    rank = np.argsort(np.argsort(z, axis=0), axis=0)
    index = np.take_along_axis(
        np.argsort(values, axis=0, kind="stable"), rank, axis=0
    )
    index[:, ~paired] = np.arange(n)[:, None, None]
    return np.take_along_axis(values, index, axis=0)

Health-zone forecasts.

The random walk models run at zone level, on the zones' own release snapshots (zone_task), with the zone, then province, then national pooling of pooling. Their zone samples are the zone model's own draws, and need not sum to the province samples (zone_forecast). The fit store makes each walk's zone run once per origin (bdbvhub.store.store.walk_zones), and every user reads it from there.

The renewal models fit the zones themselves and sum them to the provinces, and Chronos-2 forecasts the zones as series of its joint block beside the provinces and the country. Both models' zone samples are used as they are (zones_for_model). Chronos-2's need not sum to its province samples (submission.hub.zones_need_not_sum).

def check_zone_coherence(
    provinces: pd.DataFrame, zones: pd.DataFrame
) -> list[str]:
    """Check that zone samples sum to their province samples.

    Parameters
    ----------
    provinces : pandas.DataFrame
        Province samples (`SAMPLE_COLUMNS`). Values are rounded and
        clipped at zero first, as in the hub file.
    zones : pandas.DataFrame
        Zone samples (`SAMPLE_COLUMNS`).

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        One message per province and week whose zones do not sum to it
        in every sample. Empty when coherent.
    """
    keys = ["location", "target_end_date", "sample"]
    summed = (
        zones.assign(location=zones["location"].map(province_of))
        .groupby(keys)["value"]
        .sum()
    )
    prov = _final(provinces)
    want = (
        prov.loc[prov["location"].isin(summed.index.unique("location"))]
        .set_index(keys)["value"]
        .clip(lower=0)
        .round()
    )
    gap = summed.reindex(want.index, fill_value=np.nan) - want
    gap = gap.reindex(want.index.union(summed.index))
    bad = gap.loc[gap.isna() | (gap != 0)]
    return [
        f"{loc}, {week}: zone samples do not sum to the province samples"
        for loc, week in sorted({(i[0], i[1]) for i in bad.index})
    ]

def zone_task(
    task: ForecastTask,
    counts: pd.DataFrame,
    zones: tuple[str, ...],
    daily: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> ForecastTask:
    """Return the task with zones in place of provinces.

    This is how the random walk models run at zone level. Each zone gets
    a weekly series from the first week with zone data to the vintage,
    with zeros filled in.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        A province task.
    counts : pandas.DataFrame
        Weekly zone counts at the task's vintage.
    zones : tuple of str
        Zone codes. Those of the task's provinces are kept.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Daily onsets by release of the country, provinces and zones.
        The task keeps the rows of its releases for the country, its
        provinces and its zones as `daily_history`. Without it the task
        has none, so the random walk models cannot run.

    Returns
    -------
    ForecastTask
        The same weeks, vintage, delays and seed, with the zones as its
        locations and their counts as its target.
    """
    mine = tuple(z for z in zones if province_of(z) in task.locations)
    first = pd.Timestamp(counts["target_end_date"].min())
    weeks = pd.date_range(first, pd.Timestamp(as_date(task.vintage)), freq="7D")
    grid = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
        [mine, weeks.date.astype(str)], names=["location", "target_end_date"]
    )
    target = (
        counts.set_index(["location", "target_end_date"])["total"]
        .reindex(grid, fill_value=0)
        .reset_index()
        .assign(vintage=task.vintage)
    )
    history = None
    if daily is not None:
        keep = {NATIONAL, *task.locations, *mine}
        history = daily.loc[
            daily["location"].isin(keep) & (daily["vintage"] <= task.vintage)
        ].reset_index(drop=True)
    return dataclasses.replace(
        task,
        target=target,
        locations=mine,
        mask=(),
        report_by={},
        daily_history=history,
    )

def zones_for_model(samples: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:

docs.text:
JAX port of R baselinenowcast 0.2.2, with release snapshots.

Reporting triangles are (triangle, mask) pairs. mask is True where R has an observed cell and False where R has NA. The chain ladder also takes its factors from pairs of consecutive release snapshots, skipping the cells a release does not observe (delays.pair_sums); on daily releases this is R's chain ladder.

Modules: delays (the chain ladder), triangle (structure and preprocessing), aggregate (rolling sums and hub weeks), uncertainty (retrospective errors and negative binomial draws) and nowcast (the nowcast of a triangle or of release snapshots).

docs.title: nowcastbaselines.baselinenowcast.delays
docs.text:
Delay estimation by the chain ladder.

baselinenowcast's chain ladder on a reporting triangle (estimate_delay, apply_delay; Johnson, Abbott et al., the R package this ports) and the same factors from pairs of consecutive releases (pair_sums, log_factors, growth, window_pairs). The release pairs use every cell two releases both observe, so they also take releases that are batched or that begin after the onsets they report (left-truncated, as BDBV's). On daily releases the two give the same delay. fit_delay fits each place's factors at a release, pooled to its parent below MIN_LEVEL cases a week.

class Settings:
    """Settings shared by the random walk models.

    Attributes
    ----------
    max_delay : int
        $D$, the days a count may still grow, baselinenowcast's
        `max_delay`.
    min_level : float
        Cases a week for a place to use its own delay, walk spread and
        nowcast size (`pooling`).
    level_weeks : tuple of int
        First and last weeks back averaged for a place's level.
    completeness : float
        Share of a week's final count that must be reported for it to
        start the random walk.
    walk_weeks : int
        Weeks, ending at the start week, whose changes set the spread.
    start_share : float
        Share of a week reported for `randomwalknowcast` to start
        its walk from the week's nowcast.
    start_count : float
        Cases reported in a week for `randomwalknowcast` to start its walk
        from the week's nowcast.
    """

    max_delay: int = 42
    min_level: float = MIN_LEVEL
    level_weeks: tuple[int, int] = (3, 6)
    completeness: float = 0.95
    walk_weeks: int = 9
    start_share: float = 0.05
    start_count: float = 5.0

    @property
    def history_delay(self) -> int:
        """Onset days used for the delay, baselinenowcast's default.

        R uses `floor(0.5 * round(3 * D))` reference times for the delay,
        at least `D + 1`, and the rest for the uncertainty.
        """
        n_used = round(3 * self.max_delay)
        return max(n_used // 2, self.max_delay + 1)

    @property
    def retro_delay(self) -> int:
        """Days back from the origin's cut-off for retrospective nowcasts.

        R gives the `round(3 * D)` reference times left after
        `history_delay` to its retrospective nowcasts, so a release whose
        cut-off is more than this many days before the origin's gives
        none.
        """
        return round(3 * self.max_delay) - self.history_delay

def apply_delay(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    delay_pmf: Any,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Fill the unobserved cells with expected counts (R apply_delay.R:43).

    Rows are independent, so only the rows with a missing cell are
    passed to the kernel.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    delay_pmf : array_like
        Probability of each delay, as from `estimate_delay`.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        The point nowcast matrix, with no missing cells.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    pmf = jnp.asarray(delay_pmf, dtype=values.dtype)
    _validate_delay_and_triangle(m, pmf)
    k = n_unobserved_rows(m)
    if k == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "`reporting_triangle` doesn't contain any missing values, "
            "there is nothing to nowcast."
        )
    n_rows = m.shape[0]
    filled = _apply_kernel(
        values[n_rows - k :], jnp.asarray(m[n_rows - k :]), pmf
    )
    return jnp.concatenate([values[: n_rows - k], filled], axis=0)

    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    n: int | None = None,
    delay_pmf: Any = None,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Estimate the delay (unless given) and nowcast.

    R estimate_and_apply_delay.R:44.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    n : int, optional

    delay_pmf : array_like, optional
        A delay to use instead of estimating one.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        The point nowcast matrix, as from `apply_delay`.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if n is None:
        n = m.shape[0]
    if n > m.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            "The number of observations (rows) specified for delay "
            "estimation must be less than or equal to the number of rows "
            "of the reporting triangle."

    if not np.any(m[m.shape[0] - n :].all(axis=1)):
        raise ValueError(
            "The rows used for delay estimation in the reporting triangle "
            "must contain at least one row with no missing observations."
        )

    return apply_delay(values, m, delay_pmf, validate=False)

def log_factors(num: Any, den: Any, gaps: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Daily log development factors shared by all pairs (extension E1).

    A day of age $a$ at release $r$ is age $a + s$ at release $r + 1$,
    with $s$ the pair's gap in days.
    Releases are batched reports, so its growth over the gap is
    $\exp \sum_{j=a}^{a+s-1} g(j)$, with $g(j) = 0$ from ``max_delay``.
    The pairs of each gap are summed by age before the ratio, as
    baselinenowcast sums over reference times.
    Every gap and age with a denominator gives one equation
    $\log(\sum \mathrm{num} / \sum \mathrm{den}) = \sum g$,
    weighted by $\sum \mathrm{den}$, and $g \ge 0$ is the
    non-negative least squares fit.
    With a gap of 1 only, $g(a)$ is the log of the chain ladder factor.

    Parameters
    ----------
    num, den : array_like
        ``(n_loc, n_pair, max_delay)``, from `pair_sums`.
    gaps : array_like of int
        Each pair's gap in days.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        $g$, ``(n_loc, max_delay)``.
    """
    num, den = np.asarray(num, float), np.asarray(den, float)
    gaps = np.asarray(gaps, int)
    n_loc, _, d = num.shape
    uniq = np.unique(gaps)
    member = (gaps[:, None] == uniq[None, :]).astype(float)
    n_sum = np.einsum("lpa,ps->lsa", num, member)
    d_sum = np.einsum("lpa,ps->lsa", den, member)
    age = np.arange(d)
    j = np.arange(d)[None, None, :]
    lo = age[None, :, None]
    rows = ((j >= lo) & (j < lo + uniq[:, None, None])).reshape(-1, d)
    g = np.zeros((n_loc, d))
    for n in range(n_loc):
        w = d_sum[n].ravel()
        # A zero denominator gives a row of weight 0, so no equation.
        seen = w > 0
        y = np.log(np.where(seen, n_sum[n].ravel() / np.where(seen, w, 1), 1))
        root = np.sqrt(w)
        g[n] = nnls(rows * root[:, None], y * root)[0]
    return g

def growth(g: Any, start: Any, stop: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Growth $\exp \sum_{j=\mathrm{start}}^{\mathrm{stop}-1} g(j)$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : array_like
        Daily log factors, ``(n_loc, max_delay)``, from `log_factors`.
    start, stop : array_like of int
        Ages that broadcast together, clipped to ``0 .. max_delay``, so
        growth from ``max_delay`` on is 1.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        ``(n_loc, *shape)``.
    """
    g = np.asarray(g, float)
    d = g.shape[1]
    total = np.concatenate([np.zeros((g.shape[0], 1)), np.cumsum(g, 1)], 1)
    a, b = np.broadcast_arrays(
        np.clip(np.asarray(start, int), 0, d),
        np.clip(np.asarray(stop, int), 0, d),
    )
    return np.exp(total[:, b] - total[:, a])

def delay_sums(
    snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, settings: Settings, longer: bool = False
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    """Return the pair sums the delay is fitted to at release `r`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    r : int
        Release index. Pairs of later releases are not used.
    settings : Settings
        Settings.
    longer : bool
        With no in-window pair, use the pairs with a longer step, on the
        onset days of every age at their first release.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of numpy.ndarray or None
        The pairs `[P, 2]`, `num` and `den` from `pair_sums` `[L, P, D]`,
        and each pair's gap `[P]`, or None with no pair.
    """
    pairs = _pairs_at(snap, r, settings.max_delay, longer)
    if pairs.size == 0:
        return None
    counts = _delay_counts(snap, r)
    day = np.arange(snap.week.size)
    first = int(snap.cut[r]) - settings.history_delay
    gaps = snap.cut[pairs[:, 1]] - snap.cut[pairs[:, 0]]
    if (gaps > settings.max_delay).all():
        # Every age is final at the second release, so reach back
        # `max_delay` days before the first.
        oldest = int(snap.cut[pairs[:, 0]].min()) - settings.max_delay
        first = min(first, oldest)
    window = day > first
    observed = snap.observed & window[None, :]
    # The pairs are padded to a multiple of PAIR_BUCKET with copies of the
    # first, and their sums cut off after, so the compiled sums see a few
    # shapes rather than one a release.
    n = len(pairs)
    first_of = np.full(round_up(n, PAIR_BUCKET), pairs[0, 0], dtype=np.int64)
    first_of[:n] = pairs[:, 0]
    num, den = pair_sums(
        jnp.asarray(counts),
        jnp.asarray(observed),
        jnp.asarray(snap.cut),
        jnp.asarray(first_of),
        settings.max_delay,
    )
    return pairs, np.asarray(num)[:, :n], np.asarray(den)[:, :n], gaps

def fit_delay(
    snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, settings: Settings, longer: bool = False
) -> DelayFit | None:
    """Estimate the delay factors from the pairs up to release `r`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    r : int
        Release index. Pairs of later releases are not used.
    settings : Settings
        Settings.
    longer : bool
        With no in-window pair, fit the pairs with a longer step
        (`delay_sums`).

    Returns
    -------
    DelayFit or None
        The factors, or None with no pair to fit.
    """
    sums = delay_sums(snap, r, settings, longer)
    if sums is None:
        return None
    pairs, num, den, gaps = sums
    level = levels(snap, r, settings)
    pool = pool_matrix(level, snap.parent, settings.min_level)
    own_g = log_factors(num, den, gaps)
    pooled_g = log_factors(
        np.einsum("nm,mpa->npa", pool, num),
        np.einsum("nm,mpa->npa", pool, den),
        gaps,
    )
    source = source_index(level, snap.parent, min_level=settings.min_level)
    g = np.concatenate([own_g, pooled_g])[source]
    own = np.broadcast_to((source == np.arange(level.size))[:, None], g.shape)
    return DelayFit(pairs, g, level, source, np.array(own))

def truncate_to_rows(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    n: int | None = None,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> list[Triangle]:
    """Drop 1..n rows from the bottom (R truncate.R:182).

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    n : int, optional

        missing cell minus one.

        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    list of Triangle
        Element ``t - 1`` has its last ``t`` rows removed.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if n is None:
        n = m.shape[0] - n_unobserved_rows(m) - 1
    assert_integerish(n, "n", lower=0)
    out: list[Triangle] = []
    for t in range(1, int(n) + 1):
